what: Five cascaded xlat2 cycles of length 9 (N1..N5). N1 advances on every loop call; each wrap of Ni advances N(i+1). The wrap of N5 happens after exactly 9^5 = 59049 calls, prints 'Z' and halts.
why_59049: 9^5 = 59049 = 3^10, the exact modulus of the MALDOOM tick counter. Cycle length 9 exists in the xlat2 permutation (measured: cycle lengths 2,4,5,6,9,68).

counted_visits_to_N1.method: instrumented copy of the classic interpreter counts C-register visits to N1 address 58996 (from LMAO .dbg); halts at the same step count as the oracle (314258)

claim: HANDWRITTEN_MOD59049_COUNTER=DEMONSTRATED: a Classic Malbolge program, hand-written in HeLL, whose top-level cycle wraps after exactly 59049 iterations and prints Z.
limit: This is a counter modulo 59049 living in code-cell cycles; it is NOT yet a composable [d] = [d]+1 fragment on a memory word as MALDOOM's epoch contract wants.

rebuild_stability.claim: Byte-level builds are NOT reproducible (rand() fills unused cells, srand(time(NULL))); behavior is identical across builds.
rebuild_stability.note: An earlier pair of rebuilds was byte-identical by chance (same time seed). Three spaced rebuilds produce three distinct hashes. Never record an 'expected' .mb hash for LMAO output.

bolge_zig.caveat: the BOLG1 packing must strip whitespace from the .mb (the Zig VM does not strip it; malbolge.py does). With the raw file it reports input_underflow at 4256 steps; stripped, it matches exactly.
